definition: In artificial intelligence research, commonsense knowledge consists of facts about the everyday world, such as "Lemons are sour" or "Cows say moo", that all humans are expected to know.
details: It is currently an unsolved problem in artificial general intelligence. The first AI program to address common sense knowledge was Advice Taker in 1959 by John McCarthy. Commonsense knowledge can underpin a commonsense reasoning process, to attempt inferences such as "You might bake a cake because you want people to eat the cake." A natural language processing process can be attached to the commonsense knowledge base to allow the knowledge base to attempt to answer questions about the world. Common sense knowledge also helps to solve problems in the face of incomplete information. Using widely held beliefs about everyday objects, or common sense knowledge, AI systems make common sense assumptions or default assumptions about the unknown similar to the way people do. In an AI system or in English, this is expressed as "Normally P holds", "Usually P" or "Typically P so Assume P". For example, if we know the fact "Tweety is a bird", because we know the commonly held belief about birds, "typically birds fly," without knowing anything else about Tweety, we may reasonably assume the fact that "Tweety can fly." As more knowledge of the world is discovered or learned over time, the AI system can revise its assumptions about Tweety using a truth maintenance process. If we later learn that "Tweety is a penguin" then truth maintenance revises this assumption because we also know "penguins do not fly".

explainer.lead: Commonsense knowledge gives AI systems the everyday facts people usually take for granted, such as lemons being sour. It helps systems make reasonable assumptions when information is missing, although giving machines this kind of knowledge remains an unsolved problem in artificial general intelligence.

tiers.eli5: Imagine teaching a robot things everyone else already knows, like “lemons are sour” and “cows say moo.” The robot can use those facts to guess what usually happens, but it must change its guess when it learns something new. For example, it might expect a bird to fly until it discovers that the bird is a penguin.
tiers.practitioner: A system stores everyday beliefs in a commonsense knowledge base and uses them to make default assumptions during reasoning. Natural language processing can be attached so the knowledge base can attempt to answer questions about the world. Defaults must remain revisable: truth maintenance should update conclusions when new facts contradict earlier assumptions.
tiers.paperLevel: Commonsense knowledge is a collection of widely held facts about everyday objects and situations, used in reasoning patterns such as “Typically P, so assume P.” These assumptions are provisional: from “Tweety is a bird” and “typically birds fly,” infer “Tweety can fly,” then retract it after learning “Tweety is a penguin” and “penguins do not fly.” John McCarthy’s Advice Taker, introduced in 1959, was the first AI program to address commonsense knowledge; the broader problem remains unsolved in artificial general intelligence.

explainer.example: Given “Tweety is a bird” and “typically birds fly,” the system may assume that Tweety can fly. If it later learns “Tweety is a penguin” and “penguins do not fly,” truth maintenance revises the earlier assumption.

explainer.intuition: People constantly fill gaps with ordinary expectations: birds usually fly, and cakes are often baked so people can eat them. Commonsense knowledge gives an AI system similar background beliefs, while allowing it to revise its conclusions when exceptions appear.
howItWorks: Store everyday facts and widely held beliefs in a knowledge base.
When information is incomplete, apply a default such as “Usually P, so assume P.”
Use those assumptions in commonsense reasoning or question answering.
Revise earlier assumptions through truth maintenance when new facts conflict with them.
explainer.whyItMatters: Everyday statements and situations often leave important details unstated. Commonsense knowledge lets AI systems make useful default assumptions instead of stopping whenever information is incomplete, while truth maintenance limits the damage from incorrect guesses.
misconceptions: Commonsense knowledge is not the same as commonsense reasoning: the knowledge supplies facts, while reasoning uses them to draw inferences.
A default assumption is not a guaranteed fact; it can be withdrawn when new knowledge reveals an exception.
